question.problem:
Consider the function $f(x,y)$ and the region $D$ given by

$$
f(x,y)=2x+3y,\,D=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3y,\,0\le y\le 2\}.
$$

According to the mean value theorem for double integrals, there exists a point $(a,b)\in D$ such that the volume of the solid enclosed between the surface $z=f(x,y)$ and the $xy$-plane over the region $D$ equals the volume of the right cylinder with base $D$ and height $f(a,b).$ Find $a$ given that $b=1.$
question.worked_solution:
According to the mean value theorem for double integrals, there exists a point $(a,b)\in D$ such that

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A=f(a,b)\cdot \text{Area}(D).
$$

Evaluating the integral on the left-hand side, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A & ={∬}_{D}(2x+3y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3y}(2x+3y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[{x}^{2}+3xy]_{x=0}^{x=3y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}18{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =[6{y}^{3}]_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =48.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D) & ={∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{0}^{3y}\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}[x]_{x=0}^{x=3y}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}3y\,\text{d}y \\  & ={[\frac{3{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{y=0}^{y=2} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we are told that $b=1.$ So, our initial equation simplifies to

$$
\begin{aligned}48 & =f(a,1)\cdot 6 \\ 48 & =(2a+3\cdot 1)\cdot 6 \\ 8 & =2a+3 \\ 5 & =2a \\ a & =\frac{5}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $(\frac{5}{2},1)\in D.$ Therefore, the answer is $a=\frac{5}{2}.$
